title: Insider Trading Policy
date_effective: November 5, 2015 (Short Term Trading, Pre-Clearance, Section 16 Short Swing Trading Rules and Rule 144 Requirements sections effective January 1, 2016); most recently approved by the Board on January 29, 2025

tiers.name: Company Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, officers and employees of the Company or its subsidiaries, and any other person the CLO designates (e.g. a consultant, independent contractor or adviser). Subject to the fundamental insider trading and tipping prohibitions; the additional Insider-only bans (hedging, pledging, margin accounts, short sales, options, short-term trading) do not apply to this tier unless also an Insider.

tiers.name: Restricted Personnel
tiers.description: All directors, officers and salaried employees of the Company or its subsidiaries, plus any other employee, consultant, contractor or adviser the CLO designates as subject to this section. Subject to Scheduled and Additional Blackout Periods and the CLO waiver process to trade during one.

tiers.name: Insiders
tiers.description: Directors and reporting officers meeting the Section 16(a)-1(f) 'officer' definition or the Canadian NI 55-104 'reporting insider' definition. Subject to the additional prohibited transactions (short-term trading, short sales, publicly traded options, hedging, pledges, margin accounts), mandatory pre-clearance of every trade, Section 16 short-swing profit rules and Rule 144 requirements.

tiers.name: Family, household and controlled entities
tiers.description: Family members, spouses, other persons living in the household, dependent children, and partnerships, trusts, corporations or RRSPs over which any Company Personnel, Restricted Personnel or Insider exercises control or direction; each tier's rules extend to this group.

definitions.hedging_definition: financial instruments, including, for greater certainty, prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, or units of exchange funds, that are designed to hedge or offset a decrease in market value of equity securities of the Company granted as compensation or held, directly or indirectly, by the Insider

windows.start_anchor: 8:00 am (Toronto time) on the first trading day after the 14th calendar day following each fiscal quarter or fiscal year end
windows.end_anchor: after one full trading day following the formal release of the quarterly or annual financial results

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: CLO may prescribe an Additional Blackout Period from time to time due to special circumstances, covering all parties (including external advisors such as legal counsel, investment bankers and negotiation counterparties) with knowledge of those circumstances. A person told the reason for an event-specific prohibition must not disclose the reason to third parties and should avoid disclosing that the prohibition exists.

rules.section: Additional Prohibited Transactions Applicable Only to Insiders - Publicly Traded Options
rules.detail: Transactions in puts, calls or other derivative securities on an exchange or other organized market are banned outright for Insiders, other than option positions arising from hedging transactions (separately governed by the Hedging Transactions ban).
rules.evidence: transactions in puts, calls or other derivative securities by Insiders, on an exchange or in any other organized market, are prohibited by this Policy

rules.detail: An OTC put and call structured as a collar is expressly named and banned under the Hedging Transactions prohibition, regardless of whether the Company securities involved are vested.
rules.evidence: Insiders are not permitted to purchase financial instruments, including, for greater certainty, prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, or units of exchange funds, that are designed to hedge or offset a decrease in market value of equity securities of the Company

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Buying or selling puts, calls or other derivative securities is named as an example of 'trading', so it is subject only to the general insider trading/MNPI prohibition and blackout periods (if Restricted Personnel); the Insider-only bans on options and hedging do not apply.
rules.evidence: buying or selling puts or calls or other derivative securities on the Company's securities

rules.detail: Absolute ban, with no stated exception or clearance route, on hedging instruments (collars, prepaid variable forwards, equity swaps, exchange funds) over Company securities granted as compensation or otherwise held by the Insider, vested or not.
rules.evidence: the Company prohibits Insiders from engaging in such transactions

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Hedging or monetisation transactions are named as an example of 'trading' for all Company Personnel, but the outright Hedging Transactions ban applies only to Insiders.
rules.evidence: hedging or monetization transactions or similar arrangements with respect to securities of the Company

rules.detail: Prepaid variable forward contracts, the classic monetisation instrument, are named and banned alongside collars and equity swaps.
rules.evidence: prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, or units of exchange funds, that are designed to hedge or offset a decrease in market value of equity securities of the Company

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Monetisation transactions are named as 'trading' for all Company Personnel but only Insiders face the outright ban.
rules.evidence: hedging or monetization transactions or similar arrangements with respect to securities of the Company

rules.detail: Outright ban, with a narrow carve-out for cashless option exercises where the shares acquired on exercise equal or exceed the shares sold; also barred under Exchange Act s.16(c) for officers and directors.
rules.evidence: No Insider shall directly or indirectly engage in a short sale of the Company's securities

rules.detail: The short sale ban is expressly limited to Insiders; the policy does not address short selling by other Company Personnel.
Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named or addressed.

rules.section: Prohibition on Holding Securities in Margin Accounts
rules.detail: No Insider may purchase Company securities on margin or hold them in a margin account with a bank, broker or other entity, other than cashless option/SAR exercises where the exercise-price value acquired equals or exceeds the amount borrowed.
rules.evidence: no Insider shall purchase on margin or hold in a margin account with a brokerage firm, bank or other entity any securities of the Company

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Holding Company securities in a margin account is named as 'trading' for all Company Personnel, but the outright ban applies only to Insiders.
rules.evidence: holding Company securities in a margin account or pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan

rules.detail: Outright ban on pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan, because a foreclosure sale could occur while the Insider holds MNPI or is otherwise barred from trading. A narrow CLO-approved exception exists (see exceptions/financing).
rules.evidence: Insiders are prohibited from pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Pledging Company securities as collateral is named as 'trading' for all Company Personnel, but the outright ban applies only to Insiders.
rules.evidence: holding Company securities in a margin account or pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan

rules.detail: The ban on pledging Company securities as collateral is not limited to margin debt (the CLO exception process expressly excludes margin debt from its scope), so a bank loan secured on the collared shares is a prohibited secured financing arrangement absent the narrow CLO exception.
rules.evidence: An exception to this prohibition may be granted where a person wishes to pledge Company securities as collateral for a loan (not including margin debt) and clearly demonstrates the financial capacity to repay the loan without resort to the pledged securities.

rules.section: Prohibited Activities Applicable to All Company Personnel
rules.detail: Secured financing over Company securities is only expressly banned for Insiders; for other Company Personnel it is merely 'trading' subject to the general MNPI prohibition.
rules.evidence: pledging Company securities as collateral for a loan

rules.detail: An Insider who buys in the open market may not sell the same class within 6 months without pre-clearing the sale with the CLO at least 5 trading days in advance with a justification; permitted only under 'very special circumstances'. Separately, any short-swing profit within 6 months is recoverable by the Company under Exchange Act s.16(b).
rules.evidence: any Insider who purchases Company securities in the open market may not sell any Company securities of the same class during the six (6) months following the purchase without pre-clearance

rules.detail: The short-term/speculative trading restriction is expressly limited to Insiders.

clearance.approver: Chief Legal Officer (CLO); in the CLO's absence, the CFO (except the CFO's or CFO's family's own trades, which only the CEO may approve); the CLO's own or CLO's family trades must instead be approved by the CFO (or CEO in the CFO's absence); CEO/President or their family trades require both the CLO and either the Board Chair or the CFO
clearance.evidence: Insiders ... may not engage in any transaction in the Company's securities directly or indirectly ... without first obtaining pre-clearance of such transaction from the CLO. ... Unless revoked, a grant of permission will normally remain valid until the close of trading five (5) trading days following the day on which it was granted.

Every person subject to a Blackout Period who intends to trade in Securities, directly or indirectly ... during a trading restriction is required to obtain the prior approval of the CLO. The CLO may waive the application of any particular Blackout Period in respect of one or more such person(s) where the CLO has determined that it is not inappropriate, and the person(s) is/are not privy to non-public material information.

carve_outs: pre-cleared by the CLO under very special circumstances, request submitted at least 5 trading days before execution with a justification
short_term.evidence: any Insider who purchases Company securities in the open market may not sell any Company securities of the same class during the six (6) months following the purchase without pre-clearance

exceptions.evidence: An exception to this prohibition may be granted where a person wishes to pledge Company securities as collateral for a loan (not including margin debt) and clearly demonstrates the financial capacity to repay the loan without resort to the pledged securities.

exceptions.approver: CLO (Plan approval); trades thereafter are non-discretionary
exceptions.evidence: Notwithstanding any of the prohibitions contained in this Policy, Company Personnel may trade in Company securities at any time pursuant to a contract, instruction or trading plan that has been properly adopted and is properly administered in accordance with Rule 10b5-1

The receipt of common shares pursuant to vested RSUs or a similar equity award (other than through the exercise of stock options or SARs) and the exercise of a pre-arranged tax withholding right ... is exempt from this Policy.

the exercise by the Company of a pre-arranged tax withholding right pursuant to which Restricted Personnel elect to have the Company withhold and sell common shares subject to vested RSUs or other equity award to satisfy tax withholding requirements

other than in connection with "cashless" exercises of stock options under the Company's equity compensation plans and the number of securities acquired on such exercise equals or exceeds the number of securities sold

financing.minimum_shareholding_requirement: The Hedging Transactions ban is justified by reference to the Company's separate share ownership policies aligning Insiders' interests with shareholders, but no minimum shareholding requirement or hedged-share carve-out is set out in this Policy itself.

external_documents: Company's share ownership policies (referenced as rationale for the hedging ban, not set out in this Policy)
exemption_authority: CLO may grant a narrow pledge exception (financial capacity to repay without resort to the pledged securities, excluding margin debt, on 5 trading days' notice); CLO may waive a Blackout Period for a person not privy to MNPI (reported to the Disclosure Committee); CLO may pre-clear short-term trading in very special circumstances on 5 trading days' notice. No exception of any kind is provided for the Hedging Transactions, Publicly Traded Options or Short Sales bans.
jurisdiction_overlays: Canadian securities laws, including National Instrument 55-104 (Insider Reporting Requirements and Exemptions)
US Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (Section 16, Rule 10b5-1, Rule 144)

bespoke_clauses.clause: Insiders are not permitted to purchase financial instruments, including, for greater certainty, prepaid variable forward contracts, equity swaps, collars, or units of exchange funds, that are designed to hedge or offset a decrease in market value of equity securities of the Company granted as compensation or held, directly or indirectly, by the Insider.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A collar is named verbatim and banned outright for Insiders (directors and Section 16/NI 55-104 reporting officers) with no exception process at all, unlike the pledge and blackout provisions which do have narrow waivers.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Plan Creator must not enter into or alter a corresponding or hedging transaction or position with respect to the Company's securities subject to the Plan
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the loan/pledge leg were somehow structured under a Rule 10b5-1 trading plan, the plan itself would be void if it involved a hedging position, closing off that route to a collar.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any profit realized by an Insider on a purchase and sale or sale and purchase of equity securities of the Company within any six-month period belongs to and is recoverable by the Company
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Writing a call (a 'sale' of a derivative security) and later closing or settling it within six months of any matching purchase could trigger automatic US short-swing profit disgorgement for a director/Section 16 officer, independent of the outright hedging ban.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All Company securities sold by or on behalf of Insiders in the public market must be sold in accordance with the technical requirements of Rule 144, including the filing of a Form 144 with the SEC prior to or concurrently with the trade
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any market sale used to settle or unwind a collar or repay a secured loan by an Insider would separately need Rule 144 compliance and advance notice to the CLO.

summary: A funded collar is not achievable for Insiders (directors and Section 16/NI 55-104 reporting officers) under this policy: the Hedging Transactions section names and bans collars, prepaid variable forwards and equity swaps outright with no exception, exchange-traded options are separately banned, and the Pledges section bans using Company securities as loan collateral subject only to a narrow CLO-approved exception requiring proof the borrower can repay without resort to the pledged shares (and excluding margin debt from that exception). Margin accounts and short sales are also flatly prohibited for Insiders, and any short-term sale within six months of a purchase needs CLO pre-clearance granted only in very special circumstances, on top of US short-swing profit disgorgement risk. For Company Personnel who are not Insiders, none of these additional bans apply and derivatives, hedging, monetisation, margin and pledging are simply 'trading' subject to the general prohibition on dealing while aware of material non-public information and, if Restricted Personnel, quarterly blackout periods with a CLO waiver process. Since the bank's target counterparties for a funded collar (directors and senior executives) are precisely the Insiders subject to the absolute hedging and pledge-related bans, the structure is blocked for that population and would only be open, on ordinary insider-trading terms, to more junior Company Personnel who are not designated Insiders or Restricted Personnel.
